text:
elena: hey! first day here. quick practical q: if my laptop wifi drops or VPN won't auth, where do I post? and when should i ask process/"who owns this" questions in #new-hires vs the team channel? also curious how to stop onboarding-bot DMing me every hour if i want quieter reminders :wave:

onboarding-bot: welcome elena! :tada: Short answers:
- hardware/VPN/wifi -> DM @it-support or post in #help if you want teammates to see the issue. Use `/ticket create` to get a tracked ticket.
- process/who-owns -> #new-hires for cross-team questions, team channel (e.g., #eng) for team-specific ones.
- to reduce reminders DM me: `preferences quiet` or `preferences minimal`. `unsubscribe` will stop scheduled nudges entirely.
elena: thanks! any etiquette tips for minimizing noise? i don't want to flood channels in my first week.

it-support: if you file a ticket include: OS, device, error message, and run `diag collect` then attach the artifact. Example snippet to paste (redact tokens):
```
Device: elena-mbp
OS: macOS 13.4
VPN error: auth timeout (code 401)
```
That helps us triage quickly.

marc: etiquette: favor threads for follow-ups so channels stay readable. Short Qs are fine inline in #new-hires. Use reactions for simple ack (:eyes:, :thumbsup:) instead of extra messages. If it's private (salary, health, schedule) DM the person or people ops.

infra-ops: for cloud/repo access follow the access repo PR flow (link pinned in #dev-access). If you need a fast escalation add `@infra-ops` to the PR. Do not paste credentials or full keys in Slack. Use the vault or a ticket.

elena: got it — threads for follow-ups, DMs for private items, /ticket for IT. i'll DM onboarding-bot `preferences quiet` and post a 1-line intro in #introductions (PST, infra eng). thanks all! :smile:
